llm.summary: The skill is meant for Apple job searches, but it includes a generic Crawlora API helper that can call unrelated endpoints with the user's API key.

dimensions.detail: Outbound calls to https://api.crawlora.net/api/v1 with an API key are coherent with the skill's purpose and disclosed, but users should understand their job queries and IDs are sent to Crawlora.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hooks, package installation, autorun behavior, or hidden setup were found; setup is limited to obtaining and exporting CRAWLORA_API_KEY.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and reference/endpoints.md describe two Apple Jobs GET endpoints, while the bundled helper also permits generic POST bodies and arbitrary paths, so the executable capability is broader than the documented Apple-jobs workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background workers, privilege escalation, local indexing, credential harvesting, or credential storage were found; the API key is read from the environment.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is limited to searching Apple public job postings and fetching posting details, but scripts/crawlora.sh accepts arbitrary Crawlora paths and methods and includes examples for Amazon, YouTube, Google, and Google Trends.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you are comfortable sending Apple job search terms, locations, and job IDs to Crawlora with your API key. Agents using this skill should be restricted to /apple-jobs/search and /apple-jobs/job, and should not place secrets or unrelated user content in queries or POST bodies.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed: the helper's comments document unrelated Crawlora endpoints outside Apple jobs, supporting an overbroad-scope concern but not malicious intent.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed: the helper sends caller-provided paths and non-GET methods to Crawlora, which is unnecessary for the two documented Apple Jobs GET endpoints.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly downgraded: the artifact does disclose the Crawlora API base, API key header, and setup, though it lacks a fuller privacy notice about third-party handling of user-derived queries.
[E1] expected: External transmission to Crawlora is expected for this skill and documented; the concern is mainly the generic helper's ability to transmit non-Apple-job requests.
